mainTopic: Which materials are valid סכך: the wording of the bundles and haystack משניות, arrow shafts (זכרים and נקבות), stages of flax, and licorice and wormwood leaves.
overview: This amud opens in the middle of an answer. The גמרא explains that the bundles משנה says 'אין מסככין' because the problem there is only a rabbinic decree, גזירת אוצר. The haystack משנה says 'אינה סוכה' because that סוכה is invalid even מדאורייתא. Next, רב rules that זכרים arrow shafts are kosher סכך but נקבות arrow shafts are פסול. The גמרא asks 'פשיטא!' on each half and shows that each half teaches something new. Then רבי יוחנן rules on three stages of flax: combed flax is פסול, raw stalks are כשר, and he does not know the law for the middle stage, הושני. רבה בר בר חנה adds that he is not even sure what the word הושני means. Finally, רב יהודה permits licorice and wormwood leaves as סכך, while אביי forbids wormwood. The גמרא begins to give אביי's reason, and the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Different wording because one problem is rabbinic and the other is from the Torah
steps.stepSummary: The bundles משנה says 'אין מסככין' because its problem is only גזירת אוצר, which is rabbinic. The haystack משנה says 'אינה סוכה' because that סוכה is invalid even מדאורייתא, even after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Here, in the bundles משנה, where it says] that one may not roof with them, that is because of the decree of the storehouse. By Torah law it would be fine. There, in the haystack משנה, where it teaches 'it is not a סוכה,' it means even after the fact: by Torah law too, it is not a סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its answer to an earlier question. It explains why two משניות use different wording to say that a סוכה is not good.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אין מסככין' only says you should not do it in the first place. The reason is a rabbinic decree, גזירת אוצר. Sometimes a person puts his bundles on top of the סוכה to dry, as storage, and then decides to leave them there as shade. That would break the rule of תעשה ולא מן העשוי, so the חכמים banned roofing with bundles at all. 'אינה סוכה' is stronger. It means the סוכה fails even בדיעבד, because the problem there comes from the Torah itself.

keyTerms.meaning: The rabbinic decree about storage: bundles put on the roof to dry might later be left as סכך without a new act (תעשה ולא מן העשוי)
After the fact (once it was already done)

steps.whatToRemember: The wording tells you how serious the problem is. 'אין מסככין' points to a rabbinic, לכתחילה problem. 'אינה סוכה' points to a problem that ruins the סוכה even בדיעבד, from the Torah.
steps.confusionAlert: This amud begins in the middle of a sentence. The word 'הכא' (here), which refers to the bundles משנה, comes on the previous amud. So 'דְּאֵין מְסַכְּכִין' is the second half of a thought that already started.

phrases.english: [Here, where it says] that one may not roof [with them]
phrases.notes: This is the משנה about the bundles; the word for 'here' (הכא) actually appears back on the previous amud.

phrases.english: it is because of the decree of the storehouse;
but by Torah law it is fine.
There, where it teaches 'it is not a sukka,'
phrases.notes: This points to the משנה about the haystack (גדיש).

phrases.english: [it means] even after the fact:
by Torah law too, it is not a sukka.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer to a contradiction raised on the previous amud.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the two sources: one problem is rabbinic, the other is from the Torah
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two משניות seem to contradict each other about how strict the law is.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אין מסככין' means a rabbinic decree only. 'אינה סוכה' means invalid even מדאורייתא, even בדיעבד.

steps.title: רב's ruling on roofing with arrow shafts
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: a סוכה roofed with זכרים arrow shafts is כשרה, and one roofed with נקבות arrow shafts is פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: If one roofed it with 'male' arrow shafts, it is kosher. If one roofed it with 'female' arrow shafts, it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts. רב gives a ruling about using wooden arrow shafts as סכך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A 'male' shaft has a bump at its end that pushes into the metal arrowhead. It has no hollow space, so it cannot become טמא, and it is fine as סכך. A 'female' shaft has a hollow hole that the arrowhead goes into. A hollow space counts as a בית קיבול, so the shaft can become טמא, and things that can become טמא may not be used as סכך.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Male', a shaft with a bump that is inserted into the arrowhead
'Female', a shaft with a hollow hole that the arrowhead goes into

steps.whyThisMatters: This applies the basic rule that סכך must not be something that can become טמא. A wooden object with a hollow space for holding things can become טמא; a flat wooden object cannot.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
If one roofed it with 'male' arrow shafts, it is fit.
With 'female' ones, it is unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new statement. It continues the general theme of which materials are valid סכך, now dealing with wooden utensils that can or cannot become טמא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: זכרים arrow shafts are kosher סכך. נקבות arrow shafts are פסול because they have a hollow space.

steps.title: Why say the male shafts are kosher? That is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב needed to say that זכרים shafts are kosher. They are plain wood with no hollow space.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Male' shafts are kosher? That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first half of רב's ruling as unnecessary. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A male shaft is just a stick of wood with nothing hollow in it. It is no different from a regular reed. So why did רב bother to teach it?

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! (Why did it need to be said?)

phrases.english: Male ones, it is fit: that is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first half of רב's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that זכרים shafts are kosher
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Plain wood with no hollow space is obviously kosher, so the statement seems to teach nothing new.

steps.title: We might have banned male shafts because of female ones
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought the חכמים would ban זכרים shafts so that people would not confuse them with נקבות shafts. רב teaches that there is no such ban.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: let us make a decree against male shafts because of female shafts. So רב teaches us that we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב's statement does teach something new: there is no rabbinic decree against male shafts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two kinds of shafts look alike, so one could think the חכמים banned both to avoid mistakes. רב teaches that no such decree was made.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said / I might have thought
It teaches us (that this is not so)

phrases.english: Lest you say:
Let us decree against male ones because of female ones,
[so] it teaches us [that we do not].

steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows that the statement rules out a possible rabbinic decree
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Male shafts might be banned because they look like female shafts.
steps.terutzMaskana: There is no decree. Male shafts are kosher סכך.

steps.title: Why say the female shafts are invalid? That is also obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב needed to say that נקבות shafts are פסול. Every wooden object with a hollow space can become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: with 'female' shafts it is invalid. That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now challenges the second half of רב's ruling as unnecessary. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is well known that wooden objects with a hollow space for holding things can become טמא. So it seems obvious that female shafts are not allowed as סכך.

phrases.english: (The Master said:) With female ones, it is unfit:
that is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The same kind of challenge as step 3, now aimed at the second half of רב's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that נקבות shafts are פסול
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A wooden object with a hollow space can always become טמא, so the ruling seems to teach nothing new.

steps.title: A hollow that is filled permanently still counts as a hollow
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought that a hollow made to be filled once and stay filled does not count as a בית קיבול. רב teaches that it does count, so the shaft is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: a hollow space made to be filled permanently is not called a hollow space. So רב teaches us that it is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב's second statement also teaches something new: even a permanently filled hole counts as a hollow space.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A normal container gets filled and emptied again and again. The hole in a female shaft is filled by the arrowhead once and stays filled. One might think that makes it not a real container. רב teaches that it still counts, so the shaft can become טמא and is פסול for סכך.

keyTerms.meaning: A hollow space for holding things (a receptacle)
Is not called / does not count as

steps.whatToRemember: Both halves of רב's ruling teach something new. Male shafts are not banned by a decree because of female shafts. Female shafts are פסול because even a hole that is filled permanently counts as a בית קיבול.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the arrowhead 'cancels' the hollow just because it stays inside it. The point of רב's ruling is that the hole still counts as a hollow space.

phrases.english: Lest you say:
a receptacle that is made to be [permanently] filled
is not considered a receptacle,
[so] it teaches us [that it is].

steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: defines what counts as a בית קיבול
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A hollow made to be filled permanently is not a real receptacle, so the shaft cannot become טמא.
steps.terutzMaskana: It does count as a receptacle, so the shaft can become טמא and is פסול for סכך.

steps.title: Three stages of flax as סכך
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that combed flax bundles are פסול as סכך, raw flax stalks are כשר, and he does not know the law for the middle stage.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: If someone roofed a סוכה with combed flax bundles, it is פסולה. If he used raw flax stalks, it is כשרה. As for flax in the middle stage (הושני), I do not know what the law is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new statement about סכך. It lists three stages of flax, gives a ruling for two of them, and leaves the third undecided.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Combed flax is almost ready to be spun into thread, so it is treated as processed material and is פסול for סכך. Raw stalks are still in their natural state, like any plant, so they are כשר. The middle stage falls between these two, which is why רבי יוחנן is unsure.

keyTerms.meaning: He roofed it (put סכך on the סוכה)
Bundles of combed flax, ready for spinning
Flax at an in-between stage of processing
I do not know what its law is

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key idea about סכך: the more a material has been processed toward human use, the less it counts as a plain plant that may be used for roofing.

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said
Rabbi Yochanan said:
If he roofed it with bundles of combed flax, it is unfit.
phrases.notes: Combed flax is almost ready to become thread.

phrases.english: With raw flax stalks, it is fit.
phrases.notes: The stalks are still in their natural, plant-like state.

phrases.english: And flax in the middle stage, I do not know what its law is.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic. Like the arrow shafts in the steps before, it asks which materials are kosher for סכך.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אניצי פשתן is פסול. הוצני פשתן is כשר. הושני פשתן is left undecided.

steps.title: What exactly does the word הושני mean?
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה adds that he does not even know which stage of flax processing רבי יוחנן meant by the word הושני.
steps.simpleTranslation: And as for the word הושני itself, I do not know what it means. Which is it? Perhaps flax that was crushed but not combed is called הושני, while flax that was only soaked but not crushed is called הוצני. Or perhaps flax that was soaked but not crushed is also called הושני.
steps.whatsHappening: Before anyone can settle the law of הושני, רבה בר בר חנה raises a more basic problem. He is not sure which stage of flax the word refers to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Flax goes through steps: it is soaked, then crushed, then combed. The question is where the boundary falls. Option 1 says only crushed flax is הושני, so soaked flax still counts as הוצני (raw, and כשר). Option 2 says soaked flax is already הושני, so הוצני means only flax that was not processed at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Themselves; here, the meaning of the word itself

steps.confusionAlert: Here מה נפשך does not introduce a 'heads I win, tails you lose' proof, as it often does elsewhere. It simply means 'which is it?' and sets out two possible definitions of a word.

phrases.english: And the word 'hoshnei' itself, I do not know what it means.
Which is it?
Is it that if he crushed it but did not comb it,
he calls it 'hoshnei,'
but if he soaked it and did not crush it,
he calls it 'hutznei' (raw stalks)?
Or perhaps, if he soaked it and did not crush it,
he also calls it 'hoshnei.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second doubt on top of רבי יוחנן's doubt: not only the law of הושני but also its definition is unclear.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does הושני mean flax that was crushed but not combed, or does it also include flax that was only soaked?

steps.title: Licorice and wormwood leaves may be used as סכך
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that one may roof a סוכה with licorice and wormwood leaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: These licorice and wormwood leaves may be used to roof a סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling about סכך. רב יהודה permits two kinds of wide leaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People do not eat these leaves, so they are not food and cannot become טמא. They count as ordinary plants, which are valid סכך.

keyTerms.meaning: One may roof the סוכה with them

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
These licorice and wormwood leaves,
one may roof the sukkah with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה הָנֵי שׁוּשֵׁי וּשְׁווֹצְרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about which plants are valid סכך.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both licorice and wormwood leaves are valid סכך.

steps.title: אביי disagrees about wormwood
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that licorice leaves may be used as סכך, but wormwood leaves may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: One may roof with licorice leaves, but one may not roof with wormwood leaves.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a different ruling from רב יהודה. He agrees about licorice but forbids wormwood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both אמוראים agree that licorice is fine. They argue only about wormwood. Wormwood is a plant just like licorice, so אביי must have some other reason to forbid it, and the גמרא asks for that reason next.

keyTerms.meaning: One may not roof with them

phrases.english: Abaye said:
With licorice leaves, one may roof;
with wormwood leaves, one may not roof.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing ruling that partly disagrees with רב יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Licorice is valid סכך. Wormwood is not.

steps.title: Why does אביי forbid wormwood?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind אביי's ruling, and the answer begins with 'since'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why אביי forbids wormwood. This line sets up the answer, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wormwood is a plant just like licorice, so the problem is not what kind of material it is. The word כיון ('since') shows that a practical reason is coming. That reason will explain why wormwood is a problem in a סוכה.

phrases.english: What is the reason? Since…
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind אביי's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is wormwood פסול for סכך according to אביי, when licorice is כשר?
